_note: Drive data: Google Maps, fastest route from 11/8-20 Brock St Thomastown (-37.68788,145.0257629), captured 11 Nov 2026 around 4:30pm (afternoon traffic, so times are on the conservative side). Population and growth: ABS via Tom's spreadsheet (June 2025) for towns; Melbourne suburb figures are the approximate residents in the spreadsheet. LGA, landmarks and sport mix are general knowledge / judgement and are listed in README for Tom to confirm.

suburbs.name: Point Cook
suburbs.blurb: A large, fast-growing family suburb on the shores of Port Phillip Bay, and the biggest on our Melbourne list.
suburbs.sportline: Junior soccer, AFL, netball and cricket fill the local calendar, helped by the number of young families.
suburbs.occasion: junior club presentation days and primary school awards
suburbs.fact: The RAAF Museum is based at Point Cook.

suburbs.name: Craigieburn
suburbs.blurb: A major northern growth suburb on the Hume Freeway corridor, with new estates and a busy town centre.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, soccer, netball and basketball are the staples for local clubs and schools.
suburbs.occasion: end-of-season footy and netball presentations and school sports days
suburbs.fact: It is a straight run down the Hume Freeway (M31) to our showroom.

suburbs.name: Tarneit
suburbs.blurb: One of Melbourne's newest and fastest-growing western suburbs, made up largely of young families and new estates.
suburbs.sportline: Soccer, AFL, cricket and basketball are growing quickly as new clubs and school programs form.
suburbs.occasion: new club presentation nights and school end-of-year awards

suburbs.name: Pakenham
suburbs.blurb: A growing outer south-east suburb at the edge of the city, with a country-town feel and plenty of sporting clubs.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and equestrian events all feature, with country-style club days through winter.
suburbs.occasion: footy and netball club presentations, pony club days and school awards

suburbs.name: Reservoir
suburbs.blurb: A diverse northern suburb and the closest on our list to the Thomastown showroom.
suburbs.sportline: Soccer, AFL, basketball and cricket are popular with local clubs and schools.
suburbs.occasion: school presentation days and community club awards
suburbs.fact: Reservoir Primary School is one of the local schools that orders from us.

suburbs.name: Berwick
suburbs.blurb: An established, leafy south-eastern suburb with large schools and a long list of sporting clubs.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, cricket, netball and tennis are strong in the Berwick area through the year.
suburbs.occasion: school sports awards and summer cricket and tennis presentations

suburbs.name: Werribee
suburbs.blurb: The long-established centre of Melbourne's west, with a busy shopping and sporting precinct.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, soccer, cricket and athletics have deep roots in Werribee clubs.
suburbs.occasion: club champion nights, athletics carnivals and school awards
suburbs.fact: Werribee Park and the Werribee Open Range Zoo are on the doorstep.

suburbs.name: Cranbourne
suburbs.blurb: A large south-eastern suburb on the edge of the metro area, with strong local club and horse-racing traditions.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, soccer, netball and equestrian events are the mainstays of the local calendar.
suburbs.occasion: footy and netball presentations, pony club events and school awards
suburbs.fact: Cranbourne has its own racecourse and is home to the Royal Botanic Gardens Cranbourne.

suburbs.name: Glen Waverley
suburbs.blurb: A busy eastern suburb in the City of Monash, known for its schools and a busy club calendar.
suburbs.sportline: Tennis, basketball, soccer and cricket are all well supported across Glen Waverley.
suburbs.occasion: school presentation nights and tennis and basketball club awards

suburbs.name: Sunbury
suburbs.blurb: A historic township on the north-west fringe of Melbourne that has grown into a full suburb, with a country-town feel.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and equestrian are the main sports at local clubs and pony clubs.
suburbs.occasion: footy and netball presentations, pony club days and school awards

suburbs.name: Southbank
suburbs.blurb: A high-density apartment and office precinct on the Yarra, beside the CBD, with a strong corporate and hospitality mix.
suburbs.sportline: Corporate recognition, staff awards and social sports teams are the natural fit here.
suburbs.occasion: staff recognition, corporate awards and social team events
suburbs.fact: The Arts Centre Melbourne and the Southbank Promenade sit within the precinct.

drive.route: the M80 Ring Road and M2 (tolls apply)

suburbs.name: Rowville
suburbs.blurb: A family-oriented suburb in the City of Knox, with plenty of open space and neighbourhood clubs.
suburbs.sportline: Soccer, netball, cricket and golf are popular with Rowville clubs and schools.
suburbs.occasion: junior club presentations and golf day awards

suburbs.name: Narre Warren
suburbs.blurb: A major south-eastern hub in the City of Casey, anchored by a large shopping and services centre.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, basketball, soccer and netball are the busiest sports for local clubs and schools.
suburbs.occasion: winter season presentations and school sports awards
suburbs.fact: Fountain Gate shopping centre is in Narre Warren.

suburbs.name: Keysborough
suburbs.blurb: A mix of residential estates and industry in the City of Greater Dandenong, with a diverse community.
suburbs.sportline: Soccer, cricket, basketball and lawn bowls feature at community clubs.
suburbs.occasion: community club awards and lawn bowls pennant presentations

suburbs.name: Hoppers Crossing
suburbs.blurb: An established western suburb with a settled community and long-running local clubs.
suburbs.sportline: Soccer, AFL, netball and lawn bowls are staples of the Hoppers Crossing calendar.
suburbs.occasion: long-running club presentations and lawn bowls season awards

suburbs.name: St Albans
suburbs.blurb: An established, multicultural suburb in the City of Brimbank, with strong community clubs.
suburbs.sportline: Soccer, basketball, athletics and dance are important in local community programs.
suburbs.occasion: community club awards, dance concerts and school sports days

suburbs.name: Box Hill
suburbs.blurb: A major eastern hub in the City of Whitehorse, with a busy mix of shops, offices, schools and health services.
suburbs.sportline: Tennis, basketball, school sport and workplace recognition are popular around Box Hill.
suburbs.occasion: school awards, tennis and basketball club nights and workplace recognition
suburbs.fact: Box Hill Gardens and Box Hill Institute are local landmarks.

suburbs.name: Melton
suburbs.blurb: A growth-corridor township on Melbourne's western edge, with strong country-style clubs and new estates.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and equestrian events dominate the Melton calendar.
suburbs.occasion: footy and netball presentations, pony club events and school awards

drive.route: the M80 Ring Road and Melton Highway

suburbs.name: Richmond
suburbs.blurb: An inner-east suburb famous for its football heritage, close to the MCG and the sporting precinct.
suburbs.sportline: AFL, cricket and tennis lead here, with plenty of basketball from local leagues.
suburbs.occasion: footy and cricket club presentations and tennis club championships
suburbs.fact: Richmond Football Club is based at Punt Road Oval.

towns.name: Geelong
towns.blurb: Victoria's second city, on Corio Bay at the gateway to the Bellarine Peninsula and the Surf Coast.
towns.sportline: AFL and netball dominate winter, with sailing and rowing on the bay and the Barwon River.
towns.occasion: footy and netball presentations, regatta awards and school sports days
towns.fact: GMHBA Stadium at Kardinia Park is home to the Geelong Cats.

towns.name: Ballarat
towns.blurb: Victoria's largest inland city, a gold-rush heritage centre in the Central Highlands.
towns.sportline: Football, netball and rowing on Lake Wendouree lead a strong local sporting calendar.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations, rowing regattas and school awards
towns.fact: Lake Wendouree is a long-standing rowing venue in the middle of the city.

towns.name: Bendigo
towns.blurb: A large goldfields city in central Victoria, with a busy calendar of sport, arts and events.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and basketball lead the local competitions.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations, summer cricket awards and school sports days

towns.name: Shepparton
towns.blurb: The regional centre of the Goulburn Valley, surrounded by orchards, dairy and food production.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, soccer and cricket are the main sports across Greater Shepparton.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and summer cricket awards

drive.route: the Hume Freeway (M31) and Goulburn Valley Highway (M39)

towns.name: Mildura
towns.blurb: The Sunraysia hub on the Murray River, in Victoria's far north-west and joined to Buronga across the river.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and river fishing all feature in the Sunraysia sporting year.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and fishing club competitions on the Murray
towns.fact: It is the furthest of our Victorian locations from Melbourne, over 500 km away.

towns.name: Warragul
towns.blurb: A fast-growing West Gippsland town, joined with Drouin, in dairy country below the Baw Baw ranges.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and equestrian events fill the local sporting calendar.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and pony club and show days
towns.fact: It was the fastest-growing location on our Victorian list over the past ten years.

towns.name: Traralgon
towns.blurb: The largest town in Gippsland's Latrobe Valley, grouped with Morwell in the urban area figures.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, soccer and cricket are all strong across the Latrobe Valley.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and school sports days across the valley

towns.name: Warrnambool
towns.blurb: A coastal city at the western end of the Great Ocean Road, and the centre of south-west Victoria.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, equestrian and swimming all feature, with a long racing tradition.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations, racing and equestrian events and school swimming carnivals
towns.fact: The Warrnambool May Racing Carnival is held each year at the racecourse.

drive.route: the Princes Highway via the M1

towns.name: Bacchus Marsh
towns.blurb: A fast-growing valley town between Melbourne and Ballarat, in the Moorabool Shire.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and equestrian events are popular in the district.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and school awards

drive.route: the M80 Ring Road and Western Freeway (M8)

towns.name: Gisborne
towns.blurb: A growing town at the southern end of the Macedon Ranges, within commuting distance of Melbourne.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and tennis sit at the centre of local club life.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and summer cricket and tennis awards

drive.route: the M80 Ring Road and Calder Freeway (M79)

towns.name: Echuca
towns.blurb: A historic Murray River port town, grouped with Moama across the river in New South Wales.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and river fishing are staples of the local year.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and fishing club competitions on the Murray
towns.fact: The paddle steamers at the historic Port of Echuca are the town's best-known attraction.

towns.name: Moe
towns.blurb: A Latrobe Valley town, grouped with Newborough, between Warragul and Traralgon.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, soccer and lawn bowls are the mainstays of local clubs.
towns.occasion: club presentations and lawn bowls season awards

towns.name: Wangaratta
towns.blurb: A north-east Victorian town where the Ovens and King rivers meet, and a gateway to the High Country.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and cycling are the main sporting interests.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and cycling club events
towns.fact: The town hosts the annual Wangaratta Festival of Jazz and Blues and sits on the Murray to Mountains Rail Trail.

towns.name: Horsham
towns.blurb: The main town of the Wimmera, a farming region in Victoria's west on the Wimmera River.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and lawn bowls anchor the local sporting calendar.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and lawn bowls pennant awards

drive.route: the Western Freeway (M8) and Western Highway

towns.name: Bairnsdale
towns.blurb: The main town of East Gippsland and a gateway to the Gippsland Lakes.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and fishing are the staples of the East Gippsland year.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and fishing competition awards
towns.fact: The Gippsland Lakes are a major recreational fishing area.

drive.route: the Princes Freeway (M1) and Princes Highway (A1)

towns.name: Sale
towns.blurb: A Gippsland regional centre in the Wellington Shire and the gateway to the east of the region.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and golf anchor the local sporting calendar.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and golf day awards
towns.fact: RAAF Base East Sale is nearby.

towns.name: Colac
towns.blurb: A south-west Victorian town on Lake Colac, a gateway to the Otway Ranges.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and equestrian events are the main sports in the district.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations and pony club and show days

towns.name: Castlemaine
towns.blurb: A goldfields town in central Victoria with a strong arts and community scene.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, cricket and dance all feature, alongside the town's arts calendar.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations, dance concerts and school awards
towns.fact: The Castlemaine State Festival is held in the town.

towns.name: Portland
towns.blurb: A deepwater port town in Victoria's far south-west, and the state's oldest European settlement.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, sailing and fishing reflect Portland's life on the water.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations, sailing regattas and fishing club awards

towns.name: Swan Hill
towns.blurb: A Murray River town in Victoria's north-west, home to the Pioneer Settlement.
towns.sportline: AFL, netball, tennis and river fishing are the main sporting interests.
towns.occasion: football-netball presentations, tennis club events and fishing competitions
towns.fact: The Pioneer Settlement is a well-known local attraction.
